title: The scorecard says how much gate time decided nothing, for the fleet and each mission
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/history.rs (`gated`, `GateRun`: every `task.gated` with a gate time is a gate run), crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/measure.rs (`gate_time`, its parts), web/src/scorecard.ts (`dimensionParts`, the gate time card), web/src/scorecardFormat.ts and the Scorecard page's gate time cell (web/src/components/scorecard).

The problem. Compute is one of the owner's two core tracks (sync/roadmap-effects.md, "Core tracks: compute": "no machine time is spent on runs that decide nothing"). rev-b's compute study of 2026-11-11 found the gates use about 33 CPU-hours a day, about 6 of them on judgings that ended with no verdict. The live gate verdicts (read-only /api/rsi, 2026-11-12) count 12 aborted, 13 host_fault, 1 no_room and 18 stale, beside 170 accepted and 104 rejected, conflict or incompatible. The Scorecard's gate time ("15m per gate run, n 242") counts every run alike. What the gate spent on runs that decided nothing, and so whether the compute work is paying off, is on no page.

Required behaviour.
(a) Every scope's `gate_time` of `/api/scorecard` carries, beside `value`, `n` and `runs` as today:
- `total_ms`: its runs' gate times in the window, summed;
- `undecided_ms` and `undecided_runs`: the same for the runs whose verdict decided nothing (aborted, no_room, host_fault or stale).
(b) web/src/scorecardFormat.ts exports `undecidedText(gate_time)`, which reads "<undecided> of <total> gate time decided nothing (<percent>%)". A duration reads "<n>m" under an hour and "<n.n> h" from one; the percent is whole. It is null when there is no gate time.
(c) The Scorecard page shows that line under the fleet's and each mission's gate time.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/067.sh. Records are written as the integrator writes them, through `spawn_control_record`, and `spawn serve` answers. Gate mission 1's tasks 1 to 5 are judged once each: accepted (10 min), rejected (15 min), conflict (5 min), aborted (20 min) and host_fault (8 min). That is 58 min, 28 of them deciding nothing.
- (1) Through `GET /api/scorecard?since=<1 h ago>`, the fleet's and mission 1's `gate_time` are {total_ms 3480000, undecided_ms 1680000, undecided_runs 2} over 5 runs.
- (2) Under node, `undecidedText` over the fleet's reads "28m of 58m gate time decided nothing (48%)". 10 h with 1.5 h undecided reads "1.5 h of 10.0 h gate time decided nothing (15%)". Without gate time it is null.
It fails with 1 on 101077e2: the parts and `undecidedText` do not exist.

The product reason. Gate time is the fleet's scarcest compute, and the owner has made spending less of it on nothing a core goal. Saying on the page how much of it decided nothing turns the goal into a figure the owner can watch fall, and shows which mission's gates waste the most.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: scorecard tests of the parts (each undecided verdict, a run outside the window, a mission scope), and web/test tests for (b) and (c).
